text:
Alex: quick check — seeing weird behavior when a service account refreshes a JWT and the SDK routes requests to different project scopes. sometimes request goes to org A but token audience is for org B. anyone seen this?
Priya: can you paste the client config you're using? suspecting fallback logic + cached token mismatch. :thinking_face:
Alex: here's the relevant snippet from our node setup:
```js
const client = new RedwoodClient({
  auth: { type: 'service_account', keyFile: '/secrets/sa.json' },
  project: 'proj-alpha',
  scopeFallback: true, // rely on SDK to pick project scope
});
// requests sometimes end up hitting proj-beta routes (multi-tenant infra)
```
Jordan: hmm — that `scopeFallback: true` bit rings bell. fallback can reuse an existing token if it thinks audiences are compatible. if you have a short-lived cached token for proj-beta it may be reused before refresh.
Kevin: also check your refresh timing and retry behavior — if a request is retried after a 401 the SDK sometimes replays with the old token while refresh is in-flight. we had a similar race in `go` client.
Priya: quick repro steps: 1) set the local cache to have a token scoped to proj-beta. 2) make a request to proj-alpha endpoint. 3) watch logs: the SDK checks audience equality and falls back to `cachedToken` if `allowAudienceRelaxation` is true.
Alex: where is `allowAudienceRelaxation` documented? not in our internal README.
Priya: it's in auth config options — not well surfaced. example: `auth: { allowAudienceRelaxation: false }` will force strict audience match and trigger refresh immediately.
Jordan: alternative workaround: set `project`/`org` explicitly per request header to avoid ambiguous routing, e.g. `X-Redwood-Project: proj-alpha`. that short-circuits scope lookup in the router.
Alex: will that still respect token audience? worried about mismatch causing 401s.
Kevin: router will accept header but backend will validate token audience. so you need both: explicit header + strict audience enforcement so token refresh happens if mismatch.
Alex: got it. trying this patch locally now.
Priya: sample patch for node SDK to force refresh before sending when header differs:
```js
// pseudo
if (req.headers['x-redwood-project'] !== client.cachedTokenProject) {
  await client.auth.refreshToken({force: true});
}
client.send(req);
```
Jordan: small perf note — forcing refresh for every project change can spike token calls. consider caching per {(saKey, project)} tuple.
Alex: noted. do we have any test coverage for concurrent refresh races?
Kevin: CI Bot: nightly/e2e-auth-tests triggered for `auth-matrix` suite — last run: 2026-09-11 04:12 UTC. failures flagged: concurrency/test-token-race.
Alex: thanks @CI Bot — will look at that test.
Priya: tl;dr: try `allowAudienceRelaxation: false`, explicit `X-Redwood-Project` header, and short-term caching by (sa,key,project). ping me if you hit the race after that.
Alex: thanks all — i'll post results here in ~30m. :thumbsup:
